title.narrative: Support for the Accountancy Profession in Cote d'Ivoire

description.narrative: The main objectives of this IDF is to enhance the capacity of Accountancy Professional in Cote d'Ivoire to more effectively carry out its function. This will include training on accounting and auditing procedures along with reviewing the legal framework. The main objective of this IDF is to enhance the capacity of Cote d'Ivoire's professional accountancy body (Ordre des Experts Comptables et des Comptables Agrees de Cote d'Ivoire OECCA-CI) to more effectively carry out its functions as a professional institution but also as a member of IFAC. Specifically, the IDF aims to assist the OECCA-CI to (i) strengthen its legal framework with the adoption of National Auditing Standards and the establishment of an Audit Quality Review (AQR) scheme; (ii) Implement the revised version of the regional accounting standards (SYSCOA # System Comptable Ouest Africain) with regard to the IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) and support the regional professional qualification scheme developed by WAEMU since 2000.; and (iii) develop and pilot a training program for its members on the practical application of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS). All of this would result in enhancing the quality of the accounting and auditing profession and financial accountability and governance in Cote d'Ivoire.

This proposal seeks to strengthen the capacity of the Parliament in Côte d'Ivoire to effectively oversee public financial management and performance of government policies and programs. Côte d'Ivoire is emerging from a long period of political unrests and armed conflicts which has resulted in a profound deterioration of its public institutions. The Ouagadougou Peace Accord signed in 2007 between the main belligerents has paved the way for the presidential and parliamentary elections which are planned for this year. Already the reconciliation process has started to pay dividends with improved macroeconomic conditions, but there are significant institutional, political economy, and technical constraints which need to be tackled in order to sustain the economy growth and hence help break the spiral of conflict and fragility. In this context, strengthening the Parliament is critical to ensure accountability, transparency, and participation in the management of public affairs and effective delivery of public services. Indeed, parliamentary elections have not been held in Cote d'Ivoire since 2000 and it is basically by decrees that legislative and public policy decisions are being rendered. Parliament has not taken any active role in the budget formulation nor the control over the effective use of public funds. As expected, this lack of executive accountability has led to corruption and limited development impact
